name: ConocoPhillips
blurb: ConocoPhillips is the world's largest independent oil-and-gas exploration and production company by production volume, with a diversified portfolio spanning the Permian and Eagle Ford basins, Alaska, the Surmont oil-sands asset in Canada, and international positions in Norway, Qatar, and Australia. Unlike the integrated majors, COP has no refining or chemicals exposure, making its earnings the cleanest pure-play expression of upstream commodity prices among large-cap energy names.
recent: ConocoPhillips posted adjusted Q1 2026 EPS of $1.89, beating the $1.66 consensus by 14%, generating $5.4 billion of cash from operations and $2.4 billion in free cash flow despite absorbing an ~80,000 BOE/day production disruption from its Qatar operations. Production was 2,309,000 BOE/day in Q1. Management maintained full-year production guidance at 2,310,000 BOE/day but raised capital spending guidance modestly to $12.0–$12.5 billion to capture Permian efficiency gains. Notably, CEO Ryan Lance commented that the company's mid-cycle oil-price floor view is moving above the prior $65 WTI reference — a signal that sell-side models may need to ratchet higher. The Willow project in Alaska is 50% complete with early oil expected in 2029.
